subject: Mutual Action Plan: deployment mode decision & region timeline (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Gina Ramos <gina.ramos@healthnova.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Santos <alex.santos@cloudops.io>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: MAP and timeline for deployment mode + region

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the team at HealthNova is excited about Redwood's latency numbers. We're trying to lock the deployment approach and region commitments as part of our procurement timeline. To be clear on expectations, we want a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that covers:

- recommended deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for a clinical workload with PHI in EU
- evaluation plan (SLA/PT/throughput/latency targets) and acceptance criteria
- security checkpoints (SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, data residency proof)
- a close timeline and procurement steps (PO, contract redlines)

Can you share a MAP draft and an estimated schedule for a decision by July 15? Alex from our infra team is looped for technical constraints. Procurement contact is on copy for timing.

Best,
Gina Ramos
Head of Platform Integrations
HealthNova

Attachment: SOC2-snapshot-20270701.pdf (stub)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Gina Ramos <gina.ramos@healthnova.com>
Cc: Alex Santos <alex.santos@cloudops.io>, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: MAP and timeline for deployment mode + region

Gina — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely put together a MAP that separates the decision into three parallel tracks so HealthNova can choose the right tradeoffs without blocking procurement:

1) Hosted (fastest path) — Redwood hosted API, EU-only region, standard data segregation, SOC 2 controls in place; recommended for pilot when time-to-value is critical.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — customer-dedicated GPU capacity in our EU zones; predictable throughput and stronger data isolation (logical). Good for guaranteed throughput during clinical peak loads.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full private control plane, for regulated production with PHI where your legal/compliance team requires customer-managed network and HSM/KMS. Longer lead time.

I'll draft a two-week MAP with acceptance tests (latency p95 < 250ms for streaming with 1k concurrent users, throughput targets, and regression checks). Marcus (copy) will propose the eval matrix and a short perf harness.

Expect a MAP PDF and timeline by early next week (target Mon Jul 5). If you need an earlier checkpoint, we can schedule a short sync Friday.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: —

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HEALTHNOVA MAP: quick internal alignment (perf matrix + security ask)

Olga / team — draft evaluation plan below (summary):

Evaluation matrix (high level):
- Baseline dataset: 12k de-identified clinical notes (HealthNova will provide de-id subset).
- Scenarios: 1) low-latency streaming (single-turn summaries), 2) high-throughput batch embeddings (bulk), 3) KV-cache heavy chat (long-context).
- Targets: p95 latency <= 250ms streaming (EU region), sustained throughput 250 reqs/s for dedicated, degradation threshold < 10% error rate.
- Acceptance: automated smoke checks + regression prompts (we'll run your canonical prompt set).

Test harness & timeline:
- Day 0: deploy test models in Hosted EU and Dedicated EU (small pool).
- Day 1–3: run synthetic traffic + canonical prompt set; capture latency, error rates, memory/KV metrics.
- Day 4: run soak at target throughput; capture SLO violations and cost delta.
- Day 5: consolidated report and recommended deployment mode with runbook.

Data & security checkpoints (to include in MAP):
- SOC2 snapshot (attached) — Rishi to confirm shareability.
- KMS options: Hosted (Redwood-managed KMS w/ EU key residency), Dedicated (customer key in Redwood KMS tenant), Private (bring-your-own KMS / HSM).
- Connectivity tests for Private: VPN + IP allowlist verification, E2E perf impact note.

I'll produce the perf matrix CSV and an exec summary for the MAP by Monday.

Cheers,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Mutual Action Plan (MAP) & suggested decision timeline — HealthNova (HS-34567)

Hi Gina — attaching the MAP we discussed and a recommended two-week evaluation plan. High-level callouts below; full details are in the attached MAP-HealthNova-20270705.pdf.

Executive summary:
- Pilot recommendation: start on Hosted EU for fastest verification of functional parity (2-week pilot). If throughput or isolation needs exceed hosted capabilities, move to Dedicated EU (reserved GPU pools) for production. Private is available if legal mandates require customer-managed networking or HSM, but add 6–10 weeks for packaging and networking.

Key milestones (proposed):
- Jul 5: MAP sent (this email) — perf matrix and acceptance criteria included.
- Jul 6–8: HealthNova to provide de-id dataset and canonical prompt set; procurement to review PO template.
- Jul 9–13: 5-day evaluation window (Marcus to run tests).
- Jul 14: consolidated results and recommendation meeting.
- Jul 15: contractual decision & signed PO (target).

Security & compliance: SOC2 snapshot attached. For Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM and offer a deployment checklist (networking, certs, audit log shipping).

Attachments: MAP-HealthNova-20270705.pdf, SOC2-snapshot-20270701.pdf, po_template-healthnova.docx

Next steps: Can we lock the dataset delivery window (Jul 6–8)? Also propose a 30-minute results sync on Jul 14 at 10:00 AM CEST.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
